Sasha, thanks again for the call today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned as you evaluate private/on-prem options versus hyperscaler managed alternatives.

Key items we agreed to validate:
- Control plane model: fully-managed Redwood control plane vs customer-managed control plane. You flagged preference for minimal external egress; we proposed a split option where control plane sits in customer VPC with limited outbound access.
- Air-gap feasibility: confirm whether a strictly air-gapped install (no outbound internet) is necessary, or if an update window with signed artifacts is acceptable.
- Networking: NAT/firewall requirements, port ranges, and proxy support for vendor updates.
- KMS/HSM: integration with your onboarded HSM for key wrapping and model encryption.
- Tests: latency baseline (p50/p95) vs Bedrock/Vertex for same model, KV cache persistence across restarts, behavior of model-variant fallback under constrained capacity.

Attachments I will send: our private-deploy-checklist and a first-pass network diagram. Please also share any internal red-team constraints or procurement timing.

Proposed next steps:
1) Sasha to share the red-team constraints and an internal network contact (SRE).
2) We will produce two deployment patterns (split-control vs private-control-plane) with tradeoffs and a simple test plan.
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your SRE and security folks next week.

Timeline: aiming for a lightweight PoC kickoff within 2 weeks pending access and procurement.

Hi Sasha — looping in some technical detail and two concrete patterns we can offer for the PoC. Happy to run these in a lab before handing over the runbook.

Option A — Split control plane (recommended for faster onboarding):
- Control plane components run in a customer VPC or on-prem VM cluster and communicate with a minimal Redwood-managed coordination endpoint through an allowlisted outbound channel.
- Pros: quicker updates, centralized metrics, smaller customer ops burden.
- Cons: requires tightly controlled egress; not fully air-gapped.

Option B — Fully private control plane (air-gap-capable):
- All control plane services run in-customer environment. Redwood provides signed artifact bundles and an offline installer. Updates happen via an internal bastion that verifies signatures with embedded root keys.
- Pros: supports strict no-egress production; meets HSM and audit requirements.
- Cons: longer lifecycle management, scheduled maintenance windows for upgrades.

Technical validation tests we propose for the PoC:
1) Latency/throughput head-to-head: run identical request streams against Redwood Private on your hardware vs a matched instance on Bedrock/Vertex to capture p50/p95/p99.
2) Failure/recovery: restart a serving node and validate KV cache warmup and model-state rehydration without correctness degradation.
3) Update flow: simulate an offline update using signed artifacts and validate signature verification and rollback.
4) HSM integration and auditing: verify key wrapping and generate sample audit events.

Hardware minimums and logs we need for a realistic comparison: CPUs/GPUs, network topology (NAT/gateway), expected QPS distribution, average and 95th percentile sequence lengths.

Dev and I can draft a minimal runbook and an automated test harness next 48 hours if you can provide SRE contact for port access and a short list of test VMs.
